The central subject should dominate the composition. Use strong focal hierarchy: (1) the hero moment, (2) the hobby-defining object or environmental detail, (3) supporting environment or secondary objects, (4) a small delightful detail. Do not give equal visual importance to every object or environmental element in the scene, and do not spread attention evenly across the entire image. Avoid ordinary documentary composition and a cluttered scene with no clear single hero element - instead stage a single emotional or atmospheric peak. Use clean, dynamic linework, polished shading, a bright harmonious palette, subtle rim light, sparkling highlights and small glints where semantically appropriate, stylized steam/wind/dust/paper movement where appropriate, graphic color accents, lively perspective, mild perspective exaggeration, foreground framing elements, and a strong diagonal or circular visual flow when helpful - these effects should create excitement and collectibility, and must NOT turn the scene into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself requires it. Default emotional atmosphere: joyful, engaging, optimistic, energetic, curious, triumphant, exciting, inviting, aspirational; serious subjects may use tension, fascination, determination, revelation, or intellectual excitement, but should not become gloomy, depressing, muted, solemn, or dark prestige-TV realism. Prefer clean, colorful palettes, warm/cool contrast, saturated but controlled hues, a visually memorable palette identity, luminous accents, and attractive color separation between hero and background; avoid beige lifestyle palettes, muddy brown-heavy grading, monochrome editorial restraint, Western cinematic desaturation, and corporate muted color schemes. The artwork must be full-bleed and edge-to-edge. Do NOT draw a card border, white border, rounded frame, decorative frame, printed-paper edge, faux card shell, TCG layout, title bar, stats box, logo badge, corner emblem, rarity symbol, or UI panel - the application adds any card UI later; the generated image itself must be pure artwork. Do not solve a zero-human scene using invisible-human physics. Never show a tool, instrument, vessel, or object operating, pouring, swinging, or moving entirely on its own with no plausible physical cause - this reads as an erased person, not as an object-first composition. For example, never depict a watering can pouring while floating unsupported in mid-air, a racket or bat swinging with no hand and no prior momentum shown, a musical instrument playing itself with keys/strings moving with no cause. Motion must have a plausible cause such as gravity (a falling or dropped object, water pouring downward from a fixed spout under its own weight rather than tilting itself), wind or air movement (fluttering pages, drifting dust, rippling fabric), machine automation (a 3D printer head moving via its own mechanism, an automatic sprinkler, a self-stirring appliance), a ball or object already in flight from a prior, unseen action, water settling or rippling after a very recent disturbance, fire burning. An abstract system, data structure, or automated process may animate, glow, or operate entirely under its own established power/logic - no operator, hands, or controlling body of any kind may ever be implied. If an action normally requires a human hand or body to perform, do not depict the object actively performing that action by itself unless there is a visible, plausible mechanical support or automation explaining the motion (a motorized device, an automatic machine, gravity, wind, momentum already in progress, or a mechanically supported rig). Never show a kettle pouring by itself, a pen or brush writing or painting by itself, a spoon stirring by itself, scissors cutting by themselves, a microphone floating as if being held, a racket swinging itself, a camera floating as if actively taking a photo, or pages turning as if by an invisible hand. Instead, default to a resting, completed, or paused state: a kettle resting beside a finished coffee setup, a pen resting on a notebook beside already-written pages, a brush resting beside a canvas, scissors resting on a table, a microphone mounted on a stand, a racket resting on a court or bench, a camera mounted on a tripod, pages lying open naturally. Active motion is only allowed when it is physically plausible without a hand: an automated or motorized machine genuinely operating under its own established mechanism, gravity, a motorized device, wind, an object already rolling, bouncing, or falling, liquid settling after a recent disturbance, or motion that is mechanically supported and visibly explained.
